rule: Separate native document input, environment target and continuously evaluated visual state when intermediate states carry meaning.
why: Filtering an endpoint cannot recover a signature path that raw input skipped.
mechanism: User input → intent/velocity → environment target → governed travel → visual state → settle.
whenToUse: Scroll-controlled or state-controlled environments with meaningful intermediate states.
whenNotToUse: Static pages or simple content transitions whose intermediate states carry no meaning.
parameters: Travel speed, acceleration, response horizon and settle are experiment parameters.
Coordinate copy, geometry and telemetry deliberately; record intentional offsets.
dependencies: A mapping from input to target and an evaluable intermediate path.
implementationPattern: Keep raw scroll available to document controls.
Advance a separate environment travel state per elapsed time; evaluate all coupled world parameters from it.
On restored scroll initialize at the target; for reduced motion use direct intended still states.
Do not independently smooth a non-monotonic signature envelope from endpoint samples.

goodExample.claim: VELORUM refinement retained the burst peak under fast input through governed path evaluation.

antiExample.claim: Baseline VELORUM fast endpoint sweep skipped the intermediate rupture peak.
antiExample.source: VELORUM Copy/REFINEMENT_REPORT.md §2, as consolidated in evidence §9

tests: Compare slow and endpoint-fast traversal; capture the same signature states.
Reverse mid-flight; pause and resume; jump across the whole document; reload at restored scroll.
Inspect document/environment disagreement as well as callback cadence.
repairStrategy: Evaluate the meaningful path from governed travel; share semantic timing.
If catch-up hides the release behind later copy, repair handoff/reading windows without hijacking native scroll.
Add deliberate onset/settle only where it preserves agency.
cost: Small state-evaluation cost; catch-up and coupling can increase complexity.
